12.t: Working with data: how many species?
q: Which vertebrate class has the most named species?
About how many more species of birds are there than mammals?
About what fraction of all the vertebrate species shown are fish?
Total about 74 300; fish 36 000 is about 48%, close to half.
Insects alone have about 1 000 000 named species. Use this and the graph to explain why most animals are invertebrates.

All vertebrates together are about 74 000 species, while insects alone are about 1 000 000, more than 13 times as many; adding other invertebrates (worms, molluscs, spiders) means about 95% of animal species have no backbone.
